q:
At first we tried our initial strategy of ignoring, then offering another phrase to say.. but the snowball kept on rolling and my partner one day said to him that it’s a bad word and he shouldnt say it.

Needless to say, we are spiraling out of control now.
cx: A 4-year-old swearing everywhere; the partner broke the ignore plan.

q: He just does not give a damn if we take away toys or not give him ice cream or really anything.. I feel like I have 0 leverage..
cx: Same parent; consequences have stopped working.

q: I am mortified.
cx: The phrase is now said everywhere and to everyone.

q: I feel so defeated after going an activity with her after seeing so many other kids having the time of their lives.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of a nearly-3-year-old and a baby; outings end in anger.

q: I had to work so hard to make her like anything at Disney World and she loves princesses. I showed her rides and shows and everything before so she was prepared and she threw a hissy fit everyday about being there.
cx: Same mother; preparing her in advance did not help.

q: Maybe it’s more so she doesn’t like to do these things with me or her dad, but is fine with a teacher away from us?
cx: The child is calm in structured classes without her parents.

q: We are about to return to daycare and plan to go back to diapers. Should we keep training at home or just give up and try again in a few months?
cx: Two days into a 3-day Oh Crap attempt with a 26-month-old.

q:
I totally understand and was prepared for 4 days not being enough but was anticipating *some* progress that we and the daycare could work with on Monday.  
Today is day 3 and we have ZERO progress.
cx: Oh Crap over a long weekend with a 25-month-old.

q: The book says there is no such thing as a 2 y/o “not being ready” and I saw negative stories of parents giving up and trying again later with even less success
cx: What the book and other parents' stories told her about quitting.

q: She goes to daycare and we go to work so we cannot just do permanent “block 1” until it finally works so looking for alternative methods for families where Oh Crap just did not work and you did it over a longer time on a “part-time basis”
cx: The method assumes someone can stay home; both parents work.

q: Yeah, I am very tempted to just put a diaper on her and go outside to try enjoy some of the weekend. But worried that she will take it as “she won” and next attempt will be way harder
cx: Why she does not stop even though she wants to.

q: I go upstairs and she’s fine. It’s so frustrating and i don’t know what to do. I’m the problem and idk how to fix it.
cx: Breastfeeding mother; the 18-month-old cries and screams only around her, fine with the father.

q: We have no family nearby so it’s just me and husband day to day. Im SAHM 3 days of the week and those days are beginning to feel impossible. She cries and screams at me for a huge portion of the day.
cx: Same mother; she works two days and is home three.

q: She does not do this with my husband.
cx: Same mother; the father stays home with the child and they have a great time.

q: He is starting pre-K in the fall and I can’t do this anymore. I am terrified of him getting constipated so I ultimately give in and now it’s causing problems between me and my husband.
cx: 4-year-old will only poop in a pull-up; pre-K starts in the fall.

q: Same. Literally tried every damn thing
cx: Same parent agreeing with another commenter.

q: She pooped on the potty once and we had a big celebration with treats ! She was so proud. Now she seems scared of the potty.
cx: 2.5-year-old; the big celebration was followed by fear of the potty.

q: I dread coming home from work exhausted and just wanting to have a nice time st home because it's all just so much screaming and tugging at me
cx: Working mother of a 19-month-old; everything is a meltdown.

q: I'm a terrible mom, truly, and I know hating myself won't make it better but how am I supposed to get through this?
cx: Same mother asking strangers.

q: Also makes me feel like a crap mom when my kid only wants me but I also can’t make anything better.
cx: Mother who had a colicky infant and postpartum depression; a whiny day sent her back there.
